answer: A reputation system can make each agent earn influence through a bonded stake that is locked before it can vote on trades. New identities start with no weight; an agent that breaks rules loses its bond, while honest activity builds standing over time. Splitting one identity into a hundred therefore does not multiply influence: each account needs its own capital and history. The attacker pays the cost of tying up funds and risks forfeiting them, while newcomers can still wander from garden to grove and earn trust through verified work.
